newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FOCUS-Warsaw outperforms flat Central Eurobourses.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Warsaw outperforms flat Central Eurobourses.

text.p: Warsaw outperformed other east European bourses this week as prices were slack or weaker on other markets of the region.
The Central European Share Index (CESI), which reflects price movement of 50 selective Hungarian, Czech and Polish stocks, remained practically unchanged.
WARSAW

Polish shares rose this week and analysts said gains would continue, with players buying before mid-September, when some technical analysts see a rise, and before the release of firms' August earnings next week, expected to be good.

"It seems there's now a preponderance of investors who don't fear a fall," said Krzysztof Rogalski, an analyst at Bank Staropolski brokerage. On Thursday the WIG index closed at 14,010.4 points, up 442.3 points from last Friday's close.

Analysts said a good sign for stocks was that mass privatisation NFI units were flat in lower turnover on Thursday, suggesting that the units may be hitting a correction after their surge by 44 percent since late August, with some capital flowing to stocks.
BUDAPEST

Hungarian share prices advanced only modestly but intraday price movements were much wider than reflected by the weekly change of the BUX index. On Thursday the BUX index ended at 3,557.94 points, up 13.79 points over last Friday.
The week brought amendments in trading rules which traders said they still had to adapt to, but in the second half of the week once again the fundamentals took charge.
"Movements on the U.S. markets, primarily on the share market, are very important," said Robert Agoston of Daewoo Securities.
"(Hungary's) producer price inflation data were released on Thursday, consumer price inflation data will come on Friday, these will give direction for the market for one week or two."
PRAGUE

An absence of fresh factors and speculative selling in the biggest Czech banking issue Komercni Banka pushed the Prague Stock Exchange's PX50 index slightly lower during the week and dealers saw little chance of a speedy rebound.
The PX50 lost 3.8 points, or 0.65 percent, in the week to Thursday while the high cap dominated RPIX index fell five points to 1,163.
"If you look at the other main markets in the region they are not so active in general and so I expect the Czech market to follow that trend," said Karel Ruzicka of ING Barings.
Dealers said Komercni's downtrend was unlikely to have been caused by fundamental reasons and said technical factors were probably responsible.
BRATISLAVA

The insignificant trading with most of the Slovak blue chips, losses to shares of financial institutions and lack of fresh factors were behind the Bratislava Stock Exchange's several subsequent drops over this week.
The 12-share SAX index fell during the week to Thursday's close at 208.45 points, from Monday's open at 212.56 points.

"This week was characterised by more significant volumes of trade with only one blue chip, oil and gas storage firm Nafta, with most of the other bourse issues witnessing lack of interest among investors," said Peter Krutil of Creditanstalt.

Krutil said the financial institutions, mainly the country's two largest commercial banks VUB and IRB, posted a clear downward trend, initiated by domestic players, and that and the bourse needed fresh blood to reverse the current fall.
SOFIA
Six corporate issues traded on the Bulgarian stock market this week with five of them falling due to low investor interest, brokers said.
Only Varna Grand Hotel bucked the trend as it advanced two levs to 85 levs, remaining still below the 100 lev face value.
The 13-share Reuter All Bulgaria Stock Index (RABSI) closed at 41.14 points, up 0.07 from last Thursday, propelled by Varna Grand Hotel.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks traded mixed throughout the week with marginal price corrections, but traders said prices of leading issues would pick up soon, consolidating the market.

Some traders predicted a steady climb for Zagrebacka Banka due to increased demand for its shares, as well as a short term boost to confectioner Kras and food processor Podravka. But they predicted less trading with drugs firm Pliva.
LJUBLJANA
Share prices fell three percent in Ljubljana this week, which was highlighted by a "black Monday" due to the sharp plunge of financial consultancy Dadas shares.
Dadas plummeted 53.05 percent on Monday on rumours that its brokerage may be banned from trading. That pulled the SBI index down by 5.01 percent to the new all-time low at 893.88 points.
Through the week the SBI index fell 28.15 points to 912.89.
BUCHAREST
Bucharest bourse shares traded in modest volumes this week, as thin investor interest pushed most prices down.

Two independent value-weighted indices on Thursday showed drops from the previous session. The VAB, computed by Vanguard SA securities company, and the BIG, compiled by Bucharest Investment Group SA brokerage house were 5.2 percent down. Their base was 1,000 points last November.
TIRANA
Neither treasury bills nor state bonds changed hands in the four-month-old Tirana Stock Exchange during its weekly sessions on Monday and Thursday.
"Everybody chose to concentrate on the primary market, where we had an auction of treasury bills today," an exchange official said.
